# The interpreted-path catalogue (issues #169/#170) — every row
# policy.InterpretedPaths carries, and every mark shape it can render.
# Regenerate with:
#   go test ./internal/policy -update
#
# NONE OF THESE IS A REFUSAL. Every row below is a DISCLOSURE: a profile
# granting one of these paths is fully permitted, on every screen, before and
# after this table existed (issue #44). What changes is that a human reading
# --dry-run or `snug profile show` is now TOLD what the tool does with the file.
#
# class:    COMMAND TABLE (a key names a program the tool runs) or CREDENTIAL
#           (the file IS the secret). The worse of the two when both apply.
# reads:    the clause completing "the tool reads this as ___"; (none) means the
#           mark drops the clause rather than inventing an unmeasured claim.
# guest:    the mark rendered when a grant's GUEST path matches this row exactly
#           (template A for a command table, B for a credential).
# host:     the mark rendered when only the grant's HOST path matches this row
#           (template C) — the guest path is something else, but the host file
#           this row names is exposed inside anyway.
# ancestor: how this row's path reads inside a collapsed template-D line, when
#           a grant is an ancestor of several rows at once.

path:     /etc/gitconfig
class:    COMMAND TABLE
tool:     git
reads:    its system config, read with no flag
keys:     credential.helper, alias = !cmd, core.pager, core.sshCommand
evidence: measured: literal in /usr/libexec/git/git; named in `git config --system`'s fatal error. git 2.55.0. No /usr/etc/gitconfig.
guest:    ← COMMAND TABLE: git reads this as its system config, read with no flag. Read-only SUPPLIES credential.helper, alias = !cmd, core.pager, core.sshCommand.
host:     ← the host's /etc/gitconfig is exposed inside - COMMAND TABLE: credential.helper, alias = !cmd, core.pager, core.sshCommand.
ancestor: /etc/gitconfig

path:     /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json
class:    COMMAND TABLE
tool:     claude
reads:    managed (enterprise) settings, read with no flag
keys:     policyHelper, hooks, mcpServers, apiKeyHelper, env
evidence: measured: 2.1.235 bundle, getManagedFilePath + /etc/claude-code; literal x34. Full key list includes processWrapper too, dropped from Keys here to fit the mark's 60-char budget. Reads text also trimmed to fit the mark's 3-line budget; full text was "managed (enterprise) settings, the highest-precedence scope, read with no flag" — the dropped clause said it cannot be overridden by any other settings scope.
guest:    ← COMMAND TABLE: claude reads this as managed (enterprise) settings, read with no flag. Read-only SUPPLIES policyHelper, hooks, mcpServers, apiKeyHelper, env.
host:     ← the host's /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json is exposed inside - COMMAND TABLE: policyHelper, hooks, mcpServers, apiKeyHelper, env.
ancestor: /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json
